assessmentSummary.identity: Squat-to-Stand with Reach is an ordered bodyweight cycle: begin standing, hinge to contact the toes or ankles, lower/pull hips into a comfortable foot-supported squat, reach overhead in the assigned side/order, stand tall, and reset. One repetition includes the whole contact-hinge-squat-reach-stand cycle. This excludes a static Deep Squat Pry, Cossack, lateral lunge, loaded squat, assessment, locomotor flow, and forced end range.
currentCardFindings: Source 62 describes the full cycle but leaves contact choice, reach side/order, repetition boundary, support, range, fatigue, accessibility, alternate, calibration, and review contracts unspecified.

The mobility-source card `squat-to-stand-mobility-reach` has the same primary ordered cycle. One-arm versus sequential bilateral reach is an exact delivery variant, so duplicate consolidation is required after source materialization.
Five legacy YouTube URLs are retained as unverified candidate media only.

calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: No source establishes a unique Squat-to-Stand with Reach score, dose, recovery period, clinical outcome, or transfer effect.

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Materialize one candidate-only ordered Squat-to-Stand with Reach identity. Treat reach side/order, support, range, and tempo as explicit variants/modifiers. Consolidate the same `squat-to-stand-mobility-reach` cycle as a duplicate only after source materialization. Keep Deep Squat Pry, Cossack, lateral lunge, loaded squat, assessment, and locomotor flows separate.

evidence.sourceTitle: How to squat? Effects of various stance widths, foot placement angles and level of experience on knee, hip and trunk motion and loading
evidence.sourcePublisher: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
claims: Squat-to-Stand with Reach is an ordered bodyweight mobility cycle: begin standing, hinge to contact the toes or ankles, lower/pull the hips into a comfortable foot-supported squat, complete the assigned overhead reach sequence, stand tall, and reset.
This is distinct from a Deep Squat Pry that remains in the squat base, a Cossack or lateral lunge, a loaded squat, an assessment, and a flow that adds locomotion or unassigned actions.

evidence.sourceTitle: How to squat? Effects of various stance widths, foot placement angles and level of experience on knee, hip and trunk motion and loading
evidence.sourcePublisher: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
claims: The hinge-to-contact, squat entry, overhead reach, stand, and reset order are identity-critical. A one-arm versus sequential bilateral reach, support, range, tempo, and pause are declared delivery dimensions when the ordered cycle remains unchanged.
A card that omits toe/ankle contact, excludes the squat entry, or changes the terminal action cannot be automatically merged.

evidence.sourceTitle: Support moment distribution during the back squat at different depths and loads in recreationally trained females
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport
claims: Record foot, ankle, knee, hip, pelvis, trunk, shoulder, elbow, and wrist roles as task mechanics without diagnosis, tissue-isolation, or universal range claims.
Hinge, squat depth, and overhead reach alter task demands; no source establishes a universal posture, depth, or outcome for this exact flow.

evidence.sourceTitle: How to squat? Effects of various stance widths, foot placement angles and level of experience on knee, hip and trunk motion and loading
evidence.sourcePublisher: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
claims: Stance and foot angle change lower-limb and trunk motion/loading in squat tasks, so use an individually comfortable foot-supported base.
A valid cycle maintains a controlled hinge/contact, comfortable squat entry, declared reach, controlled stand, and reset; do not create range through forced lumbar motion or momentum.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Difficulty is exercise complexity and physical difficulty only; it does not classify athlete skill, proficiency, age, or readiness.
The combined hinge, squat entry, overhead reach, and stand raise coordination demand despite low external load. Independent calibration remains required.

evidence.sourceTitle: Acute effects of muscle stretching on physical performance, range of motion, and injury incidence in healthy active individuals: a systematic review
claims: Acute mobility responses depend on dose, timing, and following activity; no universal readiness, recovery, or performance outcome is claimed.
Track repetitions, reach side/order, stance, range, contact, breath, compensation, symptoms, and downstream work rather than assigning a universal recovery rule.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: A clear non-slip floor, standing and overhead clearance, optional stable support, and a safe exit are practical safeguards.
Selection uses workout inputs and the exact movement contract rather than an exercise-card participant classification.

evidence.sourceTitle: Acute Effects of Various Stretching Techniques on Range of Motion: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis
claims: No source establishes a universal Squat-to-Stand with Reach dose, depth, contact reach, rest, or readiness threshold.
Use conservative quality-limited cycles and stop before pain, pinching, dizziness, breath-holding, loss of balance, or persistent compensation.

evidence.sourceTitle: How to squat? Effects of various stance widths, foot placement angles and level of experience on knee, hip and trunk motion and loading
evidence.sourcePublisher: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
claims: Instructions must name standing setup, toe/ankle contact, controlled hip descent, comfortable squat, assigned reach side/order, stand, reset, and stop boundary.
Reduce range or use stable support before forcing contact, depth, or overhead reach.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Appropriate instruction, supervision, environment, and progressive exposure are safeguards.

Stop for sharp or increasing pain, new neurologic/circulation/breathing/dizziness symptoms, unsafe surface/support, loss of balance, inability to exit, or persistent quality loss after simplification.

evidence.sourceTitle: Acute effects of muscle stretching on physical performance, range of motion, and injury incidence in healthy active individuals: a systematic review
claims: Use Squat-to-Stand with Reach only when its exact low-load hinge-squat-reach-stand cycle fits session goals and downstream demands; it does not promise treatment, injury prevention, flexibility, or transfer.
Any change to contact, stance, support, range, reach, tempo, dose, or substitution reruns selection, logistics, duration, fatigue, and validation.

evidence.sourceTitle: How to squat? Effects of various stance widths, foot placement angles and level of experience on knee, hip and trunk motion and loading
evidence.sourcePublisher: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
claims: Athlete support should show the ordered cycle, comfortable range, breath, reach order, controlled stand, self-check, and stop prompt in plain language.
Captions, transcript, still sequence, audio description, exact variant match, and media quality remain human-review requirements.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Coach support should include floor/overhead clearance and exit checks, start/contact/squat/reach/stand verification, range and reach-side recording, compensation threshold, and escalation for unresolved symptoms.
Do not diagnose a limitation or select an adjacent squat/access drill as an automatic substitute.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Candidate accessibility supports include stable hand support, shorter range, a higher target, visual sequence cues, captions, transcript, audio description, and a reviewed task when the ordered base is inaccessible.
These supports do not establish individual readiness or preserve identity after an unreviewed task change.

evidence.sourceTitle: How to squat? Effects of various stance widths, foot placement angles and level of experience on knee, hip and trunk motion and loading
evidence.sourcePublisher: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
claims: A declared one-arm, alternating-arm, or sequential bilateral reach can be an exact variant when the contact-hinge-squat-reach-stand cycle is fixed.
Deep Squat Pry omits the stand transition; Cossack and lateral lunge change stance or foot sequence; loaded squats, assessment, and locomotor flows remain separate definitions.

Five inherited direct YouTube URLs are retained solely as unverified candidates; no playback, embedding, exact task match, captions, accessibility, quality, safety, reviewer, or approval claim is made.

alternateAssessments.name: Single-Arm Squat-to-Stand with Reach
alternateAssessments.rationale: An assigned one-arm reach changes reach-side accounting while preserving the contact-hinge-squat-reach-stand cycle.

alternateAssessments.name: Sequential Bilateral Squat-to-Stand with Reach
alternateAssessments.rationale: One reach per side before standing changes repetition duration and side accounting while preserving the ordered base cycle.

alternateAssessments.name: Supported Squat-to-Stand with Reach
alternateAssessments.rationale: Stable hand support changes balance, loading, and logistics while preserving the specified ordered cycle.

alternateAssessments.name: Slow-Tempo Squat-to-Stand with Reach
alternateAssessments.rationale: Declared tempo changes cadence only when contact, squat, reach, stand, and reset order remains fixed.

alternateAssessments.name: Squat-to-Stand Mobility Reach
alternateAssessments.rationale: The neighboring card uses the same standing hinge/toe-or-ankle contact, squat entry, overhead reach, and stand cycle; reach arm count is a delivery variant.

alternateAssessments.name: Deep Squat Pry
alternateAssessments.rationale: The task remains in a squat base with gentle pry/shift rather than executing hinge-contact-reach-stand order.

alternateAssessments.name: Cossack Squat
alternateAssessments.rationale: A fixed wide stance and unilateral lateral descent change laterality, load distribution, and primary action.

alternateAssessments.name: Lateral Lunge
alternateAssessments.rationale: A lateral step-out and return changes foot sequence and balance demands.
